title: Write-ahead checkpoint log
description: A write-ahead checkpoint log records every state transition to an append-only log before the change is applied. If the process crashes, the system replays the log from the last committed entry to rebuild the exact pre-crash state. This is the same recovery principle used by database write-ahead logs and journaling file systems. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers appending each transition to the log before applying it.

title: Periodic snapshot checkpointing
description: Periodic snapshot checkpointing saves the complete state every N operations instead of logging each one. Recovery loads the most recent snapshot and replays only the operations that came after it, which bounds recovery time. The snapshot interval trades checkpoint cost against replay cost. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers snapshotting full state every N steps.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: {"every": 4}, 2: {"every": 3}, 3: {"every": 2}}
EVERY = CFG[LEVEL]["every"]
import copy
state, snapshots, ops = {"items": []}, {}, []
for i in range(1, 11):
    op = ("add", i * 10); ops.append(op); state["items"].append(op[1])
    if i % EVERY == 0:
        snapshots[i] = copy.deepcopy(state)  # checkpoint
crash_at = 8
snap_step = max(s for s in snapshots if s <= crash_at)
restored = copy.deepcopy(snapshots[snap_step])  # resume from snapshot
for op in ops[snap_step:crash_at]:
    restored["items"].append(op[1])
print("restored:", restored["items"], "| matches:", restored["items"] == state["items"][:crash_at])

title: Idempotency-keyed resume
description: Every operation carries a unique idempotency key, and the executor records which keys have already been applied. When resuming, operations whose keys are already recorded are skipped, which guarantees each operation takes effect exactly once even if it is retried. This is the standard defense against duplicate side effects in payment and workflow systems. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers recording applied keys and skipping repeats.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Heartbeat lease checkpointing
description: Workers hold a time-limited lease on their assigned work and renew it with heartbeats while checkpointing progress. If heartbeats stop, the lease expires and a coordinator reassigns the work, resuming from the worker's last checkpoint. This keeps long jobs moving even when individual workers die silently. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers lease acquisition, heartbeat renewal, and expiry.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Differential (incremental) checkpoints
description: Differential checkpointing stores only the fields that changed since the last checkpoint instead of the whole state. Recovery folds the base snapshot and each delta in order to reconstruct the full state. This keeps checkpoint cost proportional to change volume rather than state size. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers recording per-field deltas between checkpoints.
